introduction: On this Sunday, Solomon prays for wisdom and values it more than riches. In the Gospel, a man asks Jesus what he must do to inherit eternal life; Jesus looks at him with love and invites him to sell what he has and follow him, but he goes away sad. The Letter to the Hebrews tells us that God's word is living and active. Let us ask for the wisdom to choose what lasts.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, for God all things are possible. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be free from attachment to wealth and rich in the treasure of the Gospel. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are called to leave everything and follow Christ in religious life or the priesthood: that they may answer with joy. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the rich and powerful: that they may use their wealth for the good of the poor. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the poor and all who lack what they need: that they may find generous help. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may let God's living word search our hearts and set us free. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your word is living and active. Give us the wisdom to value your Kingdom above every possession, and the freedom to follow your Son. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Jesus looking at him loved him
reflection.body:
Solomon could have asked God for anything, and he asked for wisdom. "I preferred her before sceptres and thrones. I considered riches nothing in comparison to her." True wisdom sees what really matters.

In the Gospel, a man runs up to Jesus and kneels: "Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?" He is sincere. He has kept the commandments since his youth. Then Mark adds one of the most beautiful lines in the Gospels: "Jesus looking at him loved him." Out of that love comes an invitation: "One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me."

The man cannot do it: "his face fell at that saying, and he went away sorrowful, for he was one who had great possessions." He wanted eternal life, but he was not free to receive it.

Jesus turns to his disciples: "How difficult it is for those who have riches to enter into God's Kingdom!" The disciples are astonished: "Then who can be saved?" Jesus answers: "With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God." Salvation is a gift. And to those who leave things behind for his sake, Jesus promises a hundredfold now, and eternal life.

The Letter to the Hebrews says that God's word "is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword." It sees what is in our hearts. Not everyone is called to sell everything, but everyone is called to be free.

This week, let Jesus look at you with love, as he looked at that man. Ask him: what is the one thing I lack? What am I holding on to that keeps me from following you? Then take one step toward freedom: give something away.
